title: Spike spectral-slice latency/cost runout (draft)
summary: Short draft exploring a spectral-decomposition view of short spikes (sub-500ms) across session mixes. Objective: quantify transient spike contribution to p95/p99 and dollar-per-1k-token during 1m burst windows; propose lightweight instrumentation + heuristic gating for routing/prefetch decisions.
test_setup: Workload: synthetic session mix (70% short-chat 2-6 tokens, 20% micro-turns 7-20 tokens, 10% long-turns 50-150 tokens). Models tested: open-13B-std (fp16), open-13B-q4v3 (quantized), redwood-slim-7B (optimized kernels). Hardware: H100-80GB (core region) vs A100-80GB (edge region). Duration: 4h sustained sweeps + injected 1min spikes every 10min for 2h. Metrics captured: per-request latency, enqueue time, KV cache hit, scheduling slot occupancy, per-token compute ms, billing-meter tokens. Tests run with batching disabled and with dynamic small-batch policy enabled (batch cap 8).
measurements: Representative aggregated numbers (median of 3 runs). All latencies in ms; cost in $ per 1k tokens estimated from internal cost model.

P99 composition (fraction of requests > p95 that are spike-induced):
- open-13B-std(H100): 78%
- open-13B-std(A100): 83%
- open-13B-q4v3(H100): 71%
- redwood-slim-7B(H100): 55%
analysis: Key observations: 1) Spikes dominate p99 — in our injected pattern ~70-80% of p99 mass maps to 1min spike windows for full-sized 13B variants. 2) Quantization reduces $/1kT significantly and reduces extreme spike magnitudes slightly, but the relative p99 contribution from spikes remains high. 3) Redwood-slim-7B shows materially lower spike-mean and p99 contribution (more graceful degradation), suggesting kernel-level optimizations + smaller memory footprint help during congestion. 4) A100 showed slightly worse tail behavior during spikes vs H100 for open-13B-std likely due to different kernel saturation on long sequences and scheduling preemption differences. 5) Dynamic small-batch policy smoothed p50/p95 for redwood-slim but had mixed impact on p99 for open-13B-std (introduces queuing jitter when burst density high).
conclusions:
- Short-duration spikes (1min) are a dominant factor in p99 and can inflate SLA exposure while contributing disproportionately to cost.
- Two-pronged mitigation: prefer lighter model variant for best-effort traffic, and add spike-detection gating to trigger prefetch/pin or graceful fallback to compact variants.
- Quantization remains attractive for cost but is not sufficient alone to address tail; runtime scheduling knobs and eviction/preemption policies must be tuned.
- Instrumentation suggestion: add 'spectral-slice' tag to minute-aligned windows with derived features: spike_slope, occupancy_ratio, slot_fragmentation. This is low-overhead and enables routing heuristics in console and optimize features.
recommendations:
Short term (next 2 sprints):
- Add minute-window spectral tagging pipeline (events + derived features) to observability (OPT-815).
- Run A/B: route 30% of short-chat traffic to redwood-slim during flagged spike windows for 48h; monitor p95/p99 and cost uplift.
- Evaluate quantize+kernel tune combo for open-13B on A100 to reduce spike-mean.

Medium term (quarter):
- Implement lightweight runtime gating: if spike_slope > threshold -> route to compact variant or reduce batch-cap.
- Add cost-aware rollout knob in Console to set spike routing policy per customer tier.

Cost estimates use internal cost-per-GPU-min model and do not include storage egress or networking. Related thread: slack #optimize-burst (see GH comment in linked PR).
